memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then I will remove my hand and you will see my back; but my face must not be seen.'" - Exod 33:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with a glimpse — not God's face, but where God has passed. Moses is permitted to see the trailing edge of glory, the afterward of God's presence.

That is often exactly how we experience God. In the moment, we cannot see what He is doing. It is only later, looking back, that we recognise His hand — the door that closed, the delay that protected us, the hard season that formed something in us we could not have grown any other way.

Faith is largely the willingness to trust in the middle of a story we can only understand at the end. Joseph could not see it in the pit; he saw it years later (Gen 50:20). We walk by faith, not by sight (2 Cor 5:7).

So build the habit of looking back. Remember. Write down what God has done. A memory of His faithfulness in the past is one of the strongest supports for trusting Him in the present.

And take heart: what Moses saw in shadow, we have in fullness. The Son who is the radiance of God's glory (Heb 1:3) has made Him known. And one day the glimpse will become the full sight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where can you now see God's hand in something you could not understand at the time?
2. How do you remember and record God's faithfulness?
3. What situation do you need to trust Him with before you can understand it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I cannot see what You are doing, help me trust You. Thank You for every place I can look back and see You were there. Amen.
